01_bm25.text: The battery is good at 3000MAH. The 1080p screen is brighter than my old Moto G6. The G7 is also unlocked and works on all four major US carriers AT&t Verizon Sprint and T-Mobile. So that means it will also work on all of their NVNO network carriers like Cricket, Metro by T-Mobile, Boost Mobile, Total wireless, Straight Talk, Google fi who uses Sprint's T-Mobile and US Cellular networks, and so many more. You name a carrier in the US and this Moto G7 will work on it. I am currently using my Moto G7 on Google fi. I can get the Sprint and T-Mobile networks in my area and the G7 switches automatically between them to find the best connection. My Moto G6 did not do that I had to force switch it. The G7 also as Wi-Fi calling. The unlocked Motorola Moto G7 is just an amazing phone.

I checked the IMEI #s on each carrier's website (they have Moto G7 listed as a compatible device) and it comes back as incompatible on every carrier I've tried (even the ones that allow you to purchase Moto G 7 on their site i.e. mint mobile). The customer service reps also checked the IMEI #s for the phone I just purchased and said that the device is not compatible with their networks. Save yourself the trouble and buy the US Unlocked version of the Moto G7 Power. Roughly the same exact phone, a few more $ and is compatible with the carriers listed in the title/descriptions. I tried Cricket wireless, Mint Mobile and also T-mobile directly for anyone curious. I hope this helps save someone the time and frustration.

Moto G7 with Alexa Does works with Metro, but you need to call them to connect.... Moto G7 with Alexa Does not work with Metro! Purchased on Amazon's Prime day and the phone did not connect with Metro's network. No matter what I tried and how many times and ways I tried to reset Moto G7 it was not working. I requested a replacement from Amazon and to my disappointment when it arrived it was identical to the first one. I called Motorola support line and their tech support informed me that this model is not compatible with Metro and I should switch to another carrier. Amazon describes G7 as "Moto G7 with Alexa Hands-Free - Unlocked - 64 GB - Ceramic Black (US Warranty) - Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, Sprint, Boost, Cricket, & Metro"... Buyer beware this device is not going to work on Metro. After some research it seems that the version with Alexa is the one with the issue.

best budget phone for me. i love it . it's best budget phone for me ,very quick delivered too. Fingerprint reader is good , it responds quickly. For T-Mobile sim I'm not sure it will be 4G or not. now i put my country sim which join T-Mobile network and it shows 3G. In US i use note8 with T-Mobile sim (4G) and this moto g7 with my country sim for only receiving sms. If i use internet on moto g7,i will use only wifi from hotspot not from sim. For your information.

Incompatible with T-Mobile - proof included - Moto G7 Plus (International version). See the screenshot for proof. This seems to be a great phone with one HUGE problem: it is not fully compatible with US carriers (T-Mobile in particular). Some of the calls will go directly to voicemail after long silence, and there is nothing you can do. For the calls that DO get through, network type instantly changes from LTE to 3G or even "H" (which is 2G) for the duration of the call. Bottom line: this is the international version, and it cannot reliably receive phone calls in the US. Huge disappointment. I will try a Moto G7 (not Plus, US version) and see if it is any better.

Works well with TMobile, may need tech support for ATT. Even though this phone settings show its Moto g7 plus, has Moto logo at back, and shows XT1965-T inside as model number, this had Tmobile REVVLRY+ branded "firmware" from what I was told by technical support. I have used this for few months on TMobile MVNO with no issue, but when moving to ATT MVNO in June 2022, phone wouldn't make/receive calls. It could send/receive text and get mobile data, but no voice calls. This is what was found via RedPocket technical support call. Based on the SIM number it shows as TMobile branded device rather than pure-Moto g7 Plus. So ATT-side needed SIM info to change setting on carrier side, to activate voice on the network VoLTE, especially as its listed as a compatible device on ATT website with 3G being shutdown recently.

Moto G7 plus does not work well. Bought this when it first came out right from Amazon. Moved T-mobile sim card from old phone Receives calls and makes calls but only in the US The following issues were not experienced by my family who are on the same family plan as I am and also was not experienced with my sim card in other phones. The issues are specific to the Moto G7+ I bought from this seller. text messages are delayed (both sending and receiving) When out of the US no service at all on this phone

Moto g7. The Moto g7 is a decent phone with consistent performance and quality. To increase the speed go to Settings, Accessibility, Remove animations, Turn On. Warning! Be careful the Moto g7 International models are different and are not intended for the United States. International models are missing some 4G bands for the five networks (AT&T, Sprint, T-Mobile, US Cellular, and Verizon) in the United States.

The Moto G6 has a 5.7 size screen compared to the Moto G7 6.2, so the bigger the screen, the more battery will be in use. Motorola decided to give the G7 the same 3,000mAh battery capacity as the G6 and relies on the Android Pie's Adaptive Battery feature instead of increasing the Moto G7 battery capacity to atleast 3500mAh. The Moto G7 CPU is more power efficient than the Moto G6, but not enough to offset the smaller battery for it's screen size. Compared to the Moto G7 Play and Power, Motorola decided to remove Band 71 which is a great band for T-Mobile users in rural areas and is going to be a band that T-Mobile is going to use more of. It makes no sense to have Motorola's "lesser" G7 Play and Power to have this band and not the higher spec G7.

NOT compatible with AT&T, T-Mobile, or Google Fi (soon). This phone is not compatible with VoLTE on any You.S. carrier, AFAICT. This will means that voice calls will stop working when those carriers turn off their 3G networks in early 2022.
New moto g7 user. Haven't used face or finger print

I'm just grateful the old girl held on until Black Friday when I was able to snag a Moto G7 for $179 on Amazon. The transfer of Apps and Data went smoothly and both phones had the same size SIM card (nano) so that was easy. I did have to contact my service provider and update a few mobile settings for texting but that only took a few minutes and I was up and running. "Running" is the best way to describe the past two days of putting the G7 through a battery of trials and tests. First off I was amazed at the speed and fluidity of this phone, the processor is way faster than any other Moto I've owned.

My last Motorola/Lenovo phone is still going strong after 4 years, so I expect the durability I see in the this phone's built quality will mean this G7 model lasts just as well. One snag I ran into, as I needed a nano SIM card for this G7 but had a micro SIM in my old phone. I went to the Verizon store but their system rejected the G7 as incompatible or not supported and there was no way for the store to issue me a new SIM for this G7. My local big box store has a phone kiosk and they took care of getting a me a new nano SIM card. Take-away, this G7 is Verizon compatible as advertised, but Verizon stores have some issues.

Great quality phone for the price. For the price of the Moto G7, you get a rock solid phone without breaking the bank. I've been using the G7 as my every day phone for 5 months now, and I have not had one single problem with it. Don't expect the same quality display or camera you would find on a $900+ flagship, but what the moto provides is more than enough for the average user. I've used the phone on AT&T (Cricket), T-mobile, and Verizon with no issues. This phone has done so well, I'm purchasing another as a gift to someone

I loved the phone but could not get a signal when I was at home unless I went outside in the yard and I could NOT get the WiFi Calling feature to work so I returned it. Finally I bought the Moto G7 with the US warranty. It works perfectly with my Mint Mobile sim card. The Moto G7 Power has a slightly bigger screen and a much larger battery. Unfortunately the US version of the Moto G7 Power only comes in 32GB. So I sacrificed the larger battery for additional storage with Moto G7 64GB. So the moral of the story is do not buy the international version if you live in the USA!

Walmart Family mobile. We got this phone to use on the walmart family mobile network. It works great and set up was easy. Took my sim card out my old phone and popped it in the Moto g7 and it was working right away. There was no calls to coustumer service. I really love the way it the keyboard text, speaker volume works great, smooth processing and the camera is great too. Loving this phone.

Inexpensive global phone that might work on T-Mobile or AT&T. Wonderful budget phone that might work for you if you can read the description! This is a GSM global phone. In basic English this means it will work for GSM carriers like T-Mobile and AT&T IF the towers in your area have the correct bands. From a Whistle Out article (* denotes carrier's main band; phone must be compatible with at least one main band to work on network sad Carrier AT&T: 2, 4, 5, 12*, 14, 17*, 29, 30, 66 T-Mobile: 2*, 4*, 5, 12*, 66, 71* What about budget phone carriers; MVNOs (mobile virtual network operators) like Boost and Straight Talk? They might work IF you pick a service that utilizes GSM AT&T or T-Mobile and has service in your area. Straight Talk includes SIM chips for all the networks.

Best Phone on a Budget!. If you want a new phone for a reasonable price, then this is the phone for you. The Moto G7 is a great phone to buy when you want to stay unlocked and pick the carrier you want. The phone has been working excellently and I haven't had a problem with it so far. The phone can work with all GSM Carriers (ATT, T-Mobile, Metro etc.) And CDMA Carriers. You won't regret picking this up.

It was most perplexing that all my searching found no solution, only more people with the same problem with their Moto G7. I have been a Moto G phone user for years and relied on CNET reviews of the phone which was always their favorite of the budget phones. I owned a Moto G4 initially and loved it so much I upgraded to a Moto G5 when it came out. Right now I am so glad that I kept that Moto G5 because I have put the SIM card back in it and that is my lifeline while I see what will have to be one with my newer G7. The Moto G5 is making calls and working just fine. For anyone interested, I will update this review once I have dealt with Motorola Customer Support.

Will not receive incoming calls. I’m returning this phone and getting the Moto G7. My plus model, not available in the US (because all the glitches have not been worked out per Motorola), used with a T-Mobile GSM SIM card, will not receive calls. There is no ringtone and no caller ID displayed. I’ve tried everything to include calling Motorola and my carrier (Ting) for help.

Connectivity issues, no WiFi.. Phone was good for everything except WiFi connectivity. It refused to stay connected to WiFi and was constantly searching/scanning for a new connection. Which resulted in none of the apps working. Like Alexa, Amazon shopping, etc. Constantly loading or blank screen with network error. None of my other devices had an issue so it wasn't my router. When I began researching, this is a known problem with all g7 phones, even play and power versions. Even if you turned off the scanning feature. This was under a full us warranty and Motorola costumer support was terrible. They offered to send me a used test phone as a replacement. I declined. It's a shame because it was a nice phone for all the other things.

I switched to the US version of the Moto G7 expecting better service. This time I was able to get my phone and texting to work, but had very limited success with the data. I do like the phone, but a phone that works only about 15-20% of the time in a rural area is not worth keeping. The search continues...

I have no idea. I was nervous, as I had already ordered my phone. My friend (smart thinking) told me to try his phone with my sim card from my Moto 5G. I tried my friends phone with my sim card and found that in my area I did not get LTE (we drove around for over an hour) and would esentially have a 3G at best. When my phone came, I returned my phone unopened and purchased a Moto G7 instead. I have been happy with the G7 and to be honest, I am not sure I notice the difference between my phone and my friends as far as speed, etc even though I know the specs are not the same.

LTE/3G/2G options did not work. Upgraded from Moto G5 to G7 and when we first used it, everything seemed fine. Transfer and features accessible are good for a budget phone. Went out and lost internet access. Data did not work. Went to the settings and had to figure out APN and turn to the US setting for T-mobile for data to be accessible. I believe a notice should have been provided or set to US setting when sold in the US. As this was for my daughter, she was unaware of the issue and almost returned

RETURNED AFTER 10 DAYS. I bought two of the Moto G7's to use with T-Mobile. I live in Cheyenne, Wyoming where the T-Mobile service is equal to a much bigger city. T-Mobile introduced Band 71 here in Cheyenne back in 2017 as one of two test cities for the country. So I had two main problems with the Moto G7. First of all, the signal was horrendous. I live 6 blocks from the State Capital building and couldn't get much more than 1 bar on the most of the time. If I walked into the basement, zero bars. Go outside in the backyard and Wi-Fi would drop off. Absolutely ridiculous. Yes, there is WI-FI calling so if the bars drop to zero you can still call. But really in a town that has all the T-Mobile bands? It shouldn't happen. So, the antenna used by Motorola is pretty pitiful.

Good phone. This is a budget phone enough for daily use. Moto G7 comes unlocked and works on AT&T, T-Mobile, and many other wireless carriers. Scree is big with a Full HD+ resolution. However, its battery is draining quickly. A higher mAh battery is preferred.

So I went with the 7. 3-Phone antennae is somewhat weak in the area that I live, where as the MOTO 4G was much better on the fringes. The speed of the phone is fast., and I don't experience any wi-fi connection issues. When I am on the road 4G works well with GPS feature on Google Maps. I am just not certain whether to stay with this smart phone. I have a few more days to go before I can no longer send it back to Amazon and look for something that isn't MOTO. 7/14/19 Now the MOTO 7 will not connect to my router. I have restarted the phone several times entered my password for the router and it states check password and try again. All my other devices are working but not this phone on wi-fi.

Affordable option for a TracFone compatible phone. The G7 was a replacement for an older G4 and is working fine for our needs. We aren't using facial recognition or fingerprint recognition and mostly use it for texting, calls and a little internet scrolling, so we can't comment about most features. To use with TracFone via their Verizon SIM card, you have to enter the phone's serial number to confirm that is is compatible with the Verizon network (the old G4 was not and we had service problems for three years due to poor coverage by TMobile in our area). We also have G5s in the household that we lucked out and they all worked with TracFone's Verizon SIM card, so we gambled when we bought the G7 and lucked out. Just check the TracFone site to see if the phone is compatible before opening.

Nice Phone!!. I bought the Moto G7 as an upgrade from the Moto G4. One thing that would have been good to know before buying this phone, is that the SIM card does not fit into it. I brought my old/new phone to a T-Mobile store, and they cut the SIM card to fit. The only other option would have been to purchase a 3 in 1 SIM card for $25. This is the first day of use, which is the reason I gave it 4 stars...

My last Motorola/Lenovo phone is still going strong after 4 years, so I expect the durability I see in the this phone's built quality will mean this G7 model lasts just as well. I went to the Verizon store but their system rejected the G7 as incompatible or not supported and there was no way for the store to issue me a new SIM for this G7. My local big box store has a phone kiosk and they took care of getting a me a new nano SIM card. Take-away, this G7 is Verizon compatible as advertised, but Verizon stores have some issues.

Not compatible with T-Mobile. This phone is advertised as being compatible with T-Mobile, but it is not: T-Mobile said that the phone I received is incompatible and cannot be used on their network. I purchased it directly from Amazon.

Great phone, not completely compatible, NO MOBILE DATA!!!. Text & calls work fine though. Found out, after the fact, that this is an ongoing issue between Android 9 & Sprint. I've been in some forums with others having issues with other carriers as well. Currently have an investigation open with Tello/Sprint. Will follow up with the fix if it ever happens.

Incompatible with T-Mobile - proof included - Moto G7 Plus (International version). See the screenshot for proof. This seems to be a great phone with one HUGE problem: it is not fully compatible with US carriers (T-Mobile in particular). Some of the calls will go directly to voicemail after long silence, and there is nothing you can do. For the calls that DO get through, network type instantly changes from LTE to 3G or even "H" (which is 2G) for the duration of the call. Bottom line: this is the international version, and it cannot reliably receive phone calls in the US. Huge disappointment. I will try a Moto G7 (not Plus, US version) and see if it is any better.

T-mobile issues. First off, I'd like to say this is a PREMIUM phone and I liked it for the time I had it. But from day 1 it has been a hassle with getting it to work with T-mobile. Had to call a rep to help me guide to get my network back working and to send SMS and MMS. After getting it to work after 40 mins later on a chat with a rep. The next day I could not receive or send MMS, fixed it then the next day the same issue. Its just a hassle I don't feel i should go through all this. So I'm requesting a refund. Once again, loved the phone and some of its features. Coming from a note 8 it was not a down grade. Giving it 4 out 5 stars only because of the network issues I had with it.

If it will work with your carrier. I'm not sure if it's the phone or the carrier. I've had this phone since July of 2019 and hadn't had an issue until I switched carriers. I moved to T Mobile about two months ago, at first everything was fine one month into my new carrier my phone stopped working from inside the house. I could not make or receive calls at home, everything went right to voicemail, only texts came through. I went to T mobile and the only answer was to get a cellspot for my house. It's works but I have to keep resetting it to make it work.

After some research it seems that the version with Alexa is the one with the issue. I am not sure about the one without Alexa... If you are a Metro user this is not the phone for you. ******************** I have to update this review from 1 to 4 stars for now as it was a simple issue of Metro activating (!?) unlocked phone on their network. I am puzzled by Amazon's and Motorola Mobile customer service! Very disappointing and they seem to have absolutely no clue!

Buyer beware if you are on a carrier other than the big 4. I like the phone, but I can't connect to to LTE on Ting. Don't buy unless you are on the big 4 networks or don't care about a data connection. I even contacted Motorola via chat about the issue and told to return the phone. No troubleshooting, just return the phone. I like the phone, but the connectivity problems and tech support knock it down to two stars for me.

Wifi calling feature DOES NOT work in U.S be aware!. NOT Compatable with Ting phone Service.. NOT Compatable with Ting phone Service even though its unlocked and works on the other carriers etc. Still going to use the phone for some other things over WiFi. Will return to rate starts accurately once it gets some time in.

Not compatible with Verizon in the United States. Overall, the technology on this phone was amazing! However, I bought this phone because it was advertised as US (US Warranty) compatible with Verizon networks. The phone that was shipped was a model XT1962-4, which is manufactured for the Latin American market, not the US and Canada market (XT1962-1). The XT1962-4 is actually not Verizon compatible since it's a GSM-only phone. I'm sure someone just shipped the wrong model or didn't know what they had. Buyer beware!

beware of the T Mobile problem!. Motorola website says this is compatible with T-Mobile. That is true only in certain parts of the USA. It is NOT true in NY, at least for the power g7. Motorola knows it and is not doing anything about it. Don't be fooled. Don't get this phone in NY

Inexpensive global phone that might work on T-Mobile or AT&T. Wonderful budget phone that might work for you if you can read the description! This is a GSM global phone. In basic English this means it will work for GSM carriers like T-Mobile and AT&T IF the towers in your area have the correct bands. From a Whistle Out article (* denotes carrier's main band; phone must be compatible with at least one main band to work on network sad Carrier AT&T: 2, 4, 5, 12*, 14, 17*, 29, 30, 66 T-Mobile: 2*, 4*, 5, 12*, 66, 71* What about budget phone carriers; MVNOs (mobile virtual network operators) like Boost and Straight Talk? They might work IF you pick a service that utilizes GSM AT&T or T-Mobile and has service in your area. Straight Talk includes SIM chips for all the networks.

Does NOT work with T mobile. This does NOT work with T mobile as it was advertised. The phone isn't connected to the internet at all if wifi option isn't available. I called T mobile and they told me the phone and T mobile has a compatibility issue. Why does Motorola have to lie about this? I hope they understand false marketing is illegal.
NOT VERIZON COMPATIBLE. If you did not buy it from Verizon it will not work on there network

Comes with a see through case that I plan to look for something a little sturdier/better looking. One negative is that the phone feels light for it's size and I would not want to drop it. Carrier compatibility: This phone works on Google Fi which is the most important thing for me. I live in a midsized city with good 4G coverage and so far my calls have been crystal clear and no connection issues. Previous phones and carriers have had issues with reception in my home (sound dropping out, calls dropping) and so far no issues. I have noticed that I get pushed over to HSPDA/3g for calls but that is fine for me. I generally use wifi for everything so it's not really an issue.

If you are on Boost Mobile, there may be an issue activating your phone. I was on the phone for two days to Boost Mobile and Motorola and both have advised me that there is an issue activating the phone on the Boost network. Boost needs to have the IMEI in their system, and it took three days for the problem to be resolved. Also Boost Mobile said they would have to send me a sim card that was compatible. None of the Boost Mobile sim card kits I found had the proper card, not even their own stores So if you don't want to wait for them to send you a card, go to Best Buy and get a Sprint bring your own phone sim card kit with part number SIMOLW516TQ.

Works well with TMobile, may need tech support for ATT. Even though this phone settings show its Moto g7 plus, has Moto logo at back, and shows XT1965-T inside as model number, this had Tmobile REVVLRY+ branded "firmware" from what I was told by technical support. I have used this for few months on TMobile MVNO with no issue, but when moving to ATT MVNO in June 2022, phone wouldn't make/receive calls. It could send/receive text and get mobile data, but no voice calls. This is what was found via RedPocket technical support call. Based on the SIM number it shows as TMobile branded device rather than pure-Moto g7 Plus. So ATT-side needed SIM info to change setting on carrier side, to activate voice on the network VoLTE, especially as its listed as a compatible device on ATT website with 3G being shutdown recently.

It's a beautiful phone.. I was going to upgrade my cell phone to the Moto G7 Power through my carrier, but found this one with better specs for less money and decided to buy it instead. Bought 2 phones. One was not compatible with Verizon SIM. I bought 2 Alexa enabled Moto G7s during the Prime Days sale. The phone I was going to use was incompatible with a Verizon SIM. I have initiated a return/replacement with Amazon and will update this review when I get the new phone configured for Verizon. Follow up: Amazon, sent me a replacement immediately. I was able to easily get a Verizon SIM for this phone at a Verizon store. I really, really like this phone. I'm migrating from a Galaxy S5 locked to Verizon which was getting long in the tooth.

The battery is good at 3000MAH. The 1080p screen is brighter than my old Moto G6. The G7 is also unlocked and works on all four major US carriers AT&t Verizon Sprint and T-Mobile. So that means it will also work on all of their NVNO network carriers like Cricket, Metro by T-Mobile, Boost Mobile, Total wireless, Straight Talk, Google fi who uses Sprint's T-Mobile and US Cellular networks, and so many more. You name a carrier in the US and this Moto G7 will work on it. I am currently using my Moto G7 on Google fi. I can get the Sprint and T-Mobile networks in my area and the G7 switches automatically between them to find the best connection. My Moto G6 did not do that I had to force switch it. The G7 also as Wi-Fi calling. The unlocked Motorola Moto G7 is just an amazing phone.

My plus model, not available in the US (because all the glitches have not been worked out per Motorola), used with a T-Mobile GSM SIM card, will not receive calls. There is no ringtone and no caller ID displayed. I’ve tried everything to include calling Motorola and my carrier (Ting) for help.

Bought 2 phones. One was not compatible with Verizon SIM. I bought 2 Alexa enabled Moto G7s during the Prime Days sale. We took both of them to a local Verizon store to get SIM cards (my old phone has the large format SIM and my wife had a flip phone) and while they had difficulties my wife's phone they did get it to work. The phone I was going to use was incompatible with a Verizon SIM. I have initiated a return/replacement with Amazon and will update this review when I get the new phone configured for Verizon. Follow up: Amazon, sent me a replacement immediately. I was able to easily get a Verizon SIM for this phone at a Verizon store. I really, really like this phone. I'm migrating from a Galaxy S5 locked to Verizon which was getting long in the tooth.

The battery is good at 3000MAH. The 1080p screen is brighter than my old Moto G6. The G7 is also unlocked and works on all four major US carriers AT&t Verizon Sprint and T-Mobile. So that means it will also work on all of their NVNO network carriers like Cricket, Metro by T-Mobile, Boost Mobile, Total wireless, Straight Talk, Google fi who uses Sprint's T-Mobile and US Cellular networks, and so many more. You name a carrier in the US and this Moto G7 will work on it. I am currently using my Moto G7 on Google fi. I can get the Sprint and T-Mobile networks in my area and the G7 switches automatically between them to find the best connection. My Moto G6 did not do that I had to force switch it. The G7 also as Wi-Fi calling. The unlocked Motorola Moto G7 is just an amazing phone.

Great phone, not completely compatible, NO MOBILE DATA!!!. Text & calls work fine though. Found out, after the fact, that this is an ongoing issue between Android 9 & Sprint. I've been in some forums with others having issues with other carriers as well. Currently have an investigation open with Tello/Sprint. Will follow up with the fix if it ever happens.

beware of the T Mobile problem!. Motorola website says this is compatible with T-Mobile. That is true only in certain parts of the USA. It is NOT true in NY, at least for the power g7. Motorola knows it and is not doing anything about it. Don't be fooled. Don't get this phone in NY

Comes with a see through case that I plan to look for something a little sturdier/better looking. One negative is that the phone feels light for it's size and I would not want to drop it. Carrier compatibility: This phone works on Google Fi which is the most important thing for me. I live in a midsized city with good 4G coverage and so far my calls have been crystal clear and no connection issues. Previous phones and carriers have had issues with reception in my home (sound dropping out, calls dropping) and so far no issues. I have noticed that I get pushed over to HSPDA/3g for calls but that is fine for me. I generally use wifi for everything so it's not really an issue.

Good phone with connectivity issues. Overall the phone is very nice and high quality, but I sometimes have missed calls due to lack of connection. My phone always says that I have signal and I have wifi calling enabled for my home but sometimes I'll get voicemails for calls that never got through or i'll try to make a call and it will never start ringing despite having full signal. If I turn on and off airplane mode it fixes the connection issue. I'm not 100% sure who to blame (phone or carrier) which is why i'm still giving it 3 stars, but I never had this issue on the Moto G4 i upgraded from with Metro PCS.

Inexpensive global phone that might work on T-Mobile or AT&T. Wonderful budget phone that might work for you if you can read the description! This is a GSM global phone. In basic English this means it will work for GSM carriers like T-Mobile and AT&T IF the towers in your area have the correct bands. From a Whistle Out article (* denotes carrier's main band; phone must be compatible with at least one main band to work on network sad Carrier AT&T: 2, 4, 5, 12*, 14, 17*, 29, 30, 66 T-Mobile: 2*, 4*, 5, 12*, 66, 71* What about budget phone carriers; MVNOs (mobile virtual network operators) like Boost and Straight Talk? They might work IF you pick a service that utilizes GSM AT&T or T-Mobile and has service in your area. Straight Talk includes SIM chips for all the networks.

Not compatible with T-Mobile. This phone is advertised as being compatible with T-Mobile, but it is not: T-Mobile said that the phone I received is incompatible and cannot be used on their network. I purchased it directly from Amazon.

best budget phone for me. i love it . it's best budget phone for me ,very quick delivered too. Fingerprint reader is good , it responds quickly. For T-Mobile sim I'm not sure it will be 4G or not. now i put my country sim which join T-Mobile network and it shows 3G. In US i use note8 with T-Mobile sim (4G) and this moto g7 with my country sim for only receiving sms. If i use internet on moto g7,i will use only wifi from hotspot not from sim. For your information.

NOT compatible with AT&T, T-Mobile, or Google Fi (soon). This phone is not compatible with VoLTE on any You.S. carrier, AFAICT. This will means that voice calls will stop working when those carriers turn off their 3G networks in early 2022.

I had no issues activating it on Metro by T-mobile. It will require calling in on your old phone or another line before putting the sim in the g7, but it was pain free and if you ask nicely they will waive the fee for bringing your own device. If you're on metro and have issues with LTE speeds and MMS sending, look up how to change the APN settings to the old metroPCS ones. They work better!

If you are on Boost Mobile, there may be an issue activating your phone. I was on the phone for two days to Boost Mobile and Motorola and both have advised me that there is an issue activating the phone on the Boost network. Boost needs to have the IMEI in their system, and it took three days for the problem to be resolved. Also Boost Mobile said they would have to send me a sim card that was compatible. None of the Boost Mobile sim card kits I found had the proper card, not even their own stores So if you don't want to wait for them to send you a card, go to Best Buy and get a Sprint bring your own phone sim card kit with part number SIMOLW516TQ.
